title: Negative Ext vanishing on a basis and the sheaf of derived Hom
statement: Let $f:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], let $\mathcal B$ be a basis for the topology of $Y$, and let $K,L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, where $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A basis means a family of open sets such that every open set is a union of members. Restriction to an open is induced by restricting complexes of module sheaves termwise; the module category on that open uses the restricted structure sheaf. Sheaf on $Y$ means sheaf on the site of opens with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. If $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_{f^{-1}(V)})}(K|_{f^{-1}(V)},L|_{f^{-1}(V)}[i])=0$ for every $V\in\mathcal B$ and every integer $i<0$, then the same vanishing holds for every open $V\subseteq Y$, and the assignment $V\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_{f^{-1}(V)})}(K|_{f^{-1}(V)},L|_{f^{-1}(V)})$ is a sheaf of abelian groups on $Y$.

proof.text:
Put $A=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(K,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The category of opens of each space is small in a universe containing its underlying set, and its structure sheaf is commutative, as required by the ringed-site tools below. For any open $U\subseteq X$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies $A|_U$ with $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(K|_U,L|_U)$, compatibly with successive restrictions. By the closed adjunction of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], this internal Hom is a right adjoint to $K|_U\otimes^{\mathbf L}-$ (using the tensor symmetry to put the fixed argument first). Thus clause (2) of [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model], applied on $U$, gives for every integer $i$:
$$H^i(U,A|_U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(K|_U,L|_U[i]).$$
Here $H^i(U,-)$ is derived evaluation at the whole space $U$. By [lem-sfb-unbounded-sections-localization], it is also derived evaluation of $A$ at the open $U$ of $X$. These are comparisons of abelian groups. They commute with restrictions: on a complex representative of $K$ and a K-injective representative of $L$, the comparison sends the class of a degree-$i$ cocycle of the global Hom complex to its derived morphism; the restricted target remains K-injective by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], and restricting that cocycle restricts precisely the same local module maps, and the internal-Hom restriction comparison is compatible with successive restrictions. No boundedness is needed.

source.place: Tag 0D66 (2): translate with Tags 08DK and 08DL; ringed-site versions 08JA and 08JB

proof.text: Put $B=Rf_*A$. By [lem-trf-unbounded-direct-image-section-presheaf], for every integer $i$ the presheaf $P_i(V)=H^i(f^{-1}V,A)$ is canonically isomorphic to $V\mapsto H^i(V,B)$, and $P_i^\#$ is the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal H^i(B)$. For $i<0$, Step 1 and the hypothesis say $P_i(V)=0$ for all $V\in\mathcal B$. Every map from $P_i$ to an abelian sheaf $F$ is zero: for any open $W$ and $s\in P_i(W)$, its image restricts to zero on the covering of $W$ by basis members contained in $W$, so the sheaf equalizer axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes its image zero on $W$. By the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], maps from $P_i^\#$ to $F$ are therefore unique. Set $F=P_i^\#$; its identity equals its zero endomorphism, so $P_i^\#=0$. Consequently $\mathcal H^i(B)=0$ for all $i<0$.

source.place: Tag 0D66 (1), first two sentences of proof: Tag 0D5X and vanishing of the sheafified presheaf

proof.text: Step 2 places $B$ in $D^+(\mathcal O_Y)$, since this full subcategory consists of objects with cohomology vanishing below some degree [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. The category of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules is abelian with enough injectives by [lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] with lower bound $0$ to obtain $B\cong QJ$, where every $J^n$ is injective, $J^n=0$ for $n<0$, and $J$ is K-injective. For each open $V$, the K-injective computation of the unbounded right derived functor [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] applied to evaluation at $V$ identifies $H^i(V,B)$ with $H^i(\Gamma(V,J))$.

source.place: Tag 0D66 (1), third sentence of proof; Tags 013K and 070J for the nonnegative injective model

proof.text: The section complex $\Gamma(V,J)$ is zero below degree $0$, hence has zero cohomology for $i<0$. In degree $0$, since $J^{-1}=0$, its cohomology is $\ker(\Gamma(V,J^0)\to\Gamma(V,J^1))$. Kernels in the category of module sheaves are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so this is $\Gamma(V,\ker(J^0\to J^1))=\Gamma(V,\mathcal H^0(B))$. For $V'\subseteq V$, both maps restrict the same section of $J^0$ whose differential is zero. These identifications therefore give an isomorphism of abelian presheaves $V\mapsto H^0(V,B)$ with the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal H^0(B)$, rather than merely unrelated isomorphisms of groups at each open.

source.place: Tag 0D66 (1), third and fourth sentences of proof: degree-zero section calculation

proof.text:
For every open $V\subseteq Y$, combine the comparisons of Steps 1 and 2 with Step 4:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(K|_{f^{-1}V},L|_{f^{-1}V}[i])\cong H^i(f^{-1}V,A)\cong H^i(V,B).$$
The right side is zero for $i<0$. In degree $0$ these comparisons commute with restriction, and identify the Hom presheaf in the statement with $V\mapsto\Gamma(V,\mathcal H^0(B))$. It is therefore a sheaf of abelian groups. This also handles $V=\varnothing$: module sheaves have the zero group of sections there by the empty-cover equalizer axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], so the sheaf condition includes the empty cover. No closure of $\mathcal B$ under intersections is needed: all uses of the basis were its coverings of each open by basis members contained in it.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q43-9e8730d95 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read every step and every cited statement, and made no changes. Item: its statement is Stacks 0D66(2) exactly (cohomology.tex lemma-vanishing-and-glueing, read in full): arbitrary ringed spaces, arbitrary basis, unbounded K and L, nothing weakened. It is a real lemma used by the parent's Step 3, not a restated clause of the parent. Step 1 makes 08DK precise: the internal-Hom restriction node, the closed adjunction plus the symmetry, clause (2) of the derived-internal-Hom sections-model node, the slice-localization node and K-injective restriction. Together these give an isomorphism of presheaves with H^i(f^-1V, RHom(K,L)). Step 2 is the vanishing-on-a-basis argument: equalizer axiom plus the sheafification universal property, so P_i^#=0. It needs neither intersections of basis opens nor a basis on X. Step 3 uses D^+ membership, enough injectives on Y and the dplus representative with n=0 and K-injective J, so H^i(V,B)=H^i(J(V)). Step 4: J^-1=0 and kernels are sectionwise, so H^0(V,B)=Gamma(V,H^0 B), compatibly with restriction. Step 5 chains these; the empty open is covered. New node lem-trf-unbounded-direct-image-section-presheaf: exactly Stacks 0D5X together with the 0D5W Leray comparison (read at cohomology.tex 7917-7956), with the same hypotheses. Tested on a point and on f=id, including negative q. It is statement-only and self-contained, and has LeanFinder, LeanSearch, Loogle and grep searches. My own rg over the DAG (0D5X, 0D5W, 0D6I, 0BKJ, Leray, sheafification and direct image) and over the main and master blueprints found only scheme, pro-etale, qcoh or single-sheaf versions, so the node is not a duplicate.
